pull_request.title: Calorimeter: compare tiled ECAL with continuous sector silicon
pull_request.head: codex/ecal10k-untiled-control
pull_request.body:
The original tiled ECAL sample has broad angular raw-response distributions. This adds a deliberately unbuildable control with continuous 0.5 mm sensitive silicon across each existing sector carrier face and reruns the exact same 10,000 electron primary records with 12 DDSim workers, seeds and physics settings. Follow-up to #134; no production detector or design-approval change.

The paired overlays show |eta| widths falling from 27.95–55.78% to 9.41–16.46%; folded-phi interior bins from 22.59–25.32% to 3.69–4.10%; and seam-adjacent bins from 110.31/110.09% to 27.22/27.26%. All twenty direct tiled-minus-continuous 95% paired-bootstrap intervals are positive. Mean response and all underlying angular populations accompany the widths; zero responses remain included (42 tiled, 37 continuous). The observable is sample SD(R)/mean(R), R = raw silicon deposit / true energy, rather than intrinsic fixed-energy reconstructed resolution.

The XML-only control reuses unchanged native factories and audit libraries, retains inherited sector seams, layer planes, absorber and other passive material, and explicitly subtracts support intersections at silicon planes. It adds 2,475.64 kg of silicon and removes 447.43 kg of aluminium. Thus the result measures this coverage/material counterfactual, including guards, module gaps and service margins together; it does not define a separable electronics or tiling variance term.

Validation: 18 geometry/statistical controls; 2,304 native sheets and unique volume IDs; 3,136 wide-address checks; zero native overlaps/extrusions at 1e-5 mm; 24-event/12-worker pilot; full 10,000-primary and 10,006,736-hit readback; exact primary pairing and unchanged original twenty moments; 5,000 paired whole-event bootstrap replicas with finite symmetric positive-definite 40-width and 20-difference covariance; visual plot inspection; separate PhysVal source/result assessments; project, inventory, session/interaction/token validators and token-site build. Full transport took 1514.572 s, used 2.302 GiB peak RSS and wrote 13.146 GB. About 385 GiB remains free; no sample reduction was needed.

Only recipes, figures, compact binwise evidence and curated records are published. Raw ROOT, exact primary/event ledgers, full per-part geometry ledger and bulky logs remain local and ignored. No engineering acceptance or intrinsic-resolution claim. Exact task token counters are unavailable.

![Tiled versus continuous silicon response widths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asalzburger/nodd/9ec0abf613f87c13492c900d0e7f573329d6f27a/docs/validation/ecal10k-untiled/results/resolution-overlay.png)

|---|---:|---:|
| Absolute eta bins | 28–56% | 9–16% |

The width is sample SD(R)/mean(R), with R = silicon energy / true primary energy. Bars show 95% paired whole-event bootstrap intervals. The user said: “Please go ahead with these tests.” This follows the proposed
local-position calibration and independent module-phase tests in PR135. The
bounded implementation uses identical retained 10,000 electron inputs and
12 DDSim workers, with disk planning and a live guard. Starting revision:
`3af5538faf884d0abce98b0956c0e6d4f45d4527`; clean dedicated branch
`codex/ecal-calibration-staggering-tests`. Earlier samples remain unchanged.
The repository is the canonical record. This is an isolated PROTOTYPE under
DES-030/DES-031; no human sign-off or production integration is inferred.

The coordinator applied `nodd-coordinate`, `nodd-design-evidence`,
`nodd-review-validation` and the local ACTS Spack skill. Changed setup/lock
fingerprints were disclosed before dependent work; the native runtime doctor
passed. Existing dependencies were reused without modifying shared installs.

events.text:
The physical four-phase board layout was frozen before response inspection.
Barrel narrow edge boards preserve envelopes/ASIC capacity; short slabs use a
24 mm quarter-phase to preserve rows/clearance. All area/material changes are
explicit. Native construction/IDs/electrodes/zero-overlap checks, 24-event pilot,
full 10k transport and all saved-primary/hit/12-worker audits pass. The original
sector seams remain. Dense mask screening is geometry only.

The calibration protocol freezes observable-only features, five outer/three
inner ID folds, training-only preprocessing, ridge candidates and gain bounds.
Separate `Model.infer(features, signal)` returns energy without truth inputs;
held-out truth changes leave inferred energy unchanged. No held-out retuning.
The first baseline fit improves global CV from 43.09% to 34.43%, while retaining
mean Ecal/Etrue=0.9136 and 8.99% clipping. This scale bias is a reported limitation,
not removed by an evaluation-derived correction. Final paired analysis follows.

events.text:
Yes. I would pursue **a local response correction and independent board staggering**, then measure their gains separately.

1. **Calibration based on reconstructed position**

   Fit the mean response \(f=\langle E_{\rm Si}/E_{\rm true}\rangle\) versus reconstructed impact position and distance to sensor gaps, service bays and sector seams. Apply:
   \[
   E_{\rm cal}=E_{\rm Si}/\hat f.
   \]
   Start with smooth, low-dimensional maps for barrel and endcaps. Add longitudinal shower information if it improves validation.

   Train and evaluate on separate events; true energy supplies training labels, while inference uses reconstructed observables. Check energy-scale closure in narrow energy slices, tails and zero-response fractions.

   **One constant correction per displayed angular bin leaves that bin’s σ/mean unchanged.** We need finer position information. Calibration can correct predictable losses, but missing shower fluctuations and zero signals remain limitations. CALICE demonstrated this kind of barycentre-dependent gap correction and documented its residual fluctuations. [CALICE, §5.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0811.2354)

2. **Stagger the board grid independently of the slab joints**

   The current barrel already uses **−96/+96 mm slab shifts**, but those differ by **two 96 mm board pitches**. They move service joints while preserving the interior board-grid phase.

   I would test a four-layer cycle of tangential/axial board phases:
   **(0,0), (48,0), (0,48), (48,48) mm**.

   Keep the existing slab-joint staggering separately. The packing check suggests axial shifts away from service bays can retain nine boards in full slabs. Tangential shifts require partial edge boards or repacking; short slabs also need separate treatment. Endcaps should use complementary layer-dependent layouts instead of repeating one mask through all 48 layers.

   **Sector cracks need a larger mechanical change:** stepped or nonprojective joints whose position changes with depth, so a radial trajectory cannot follow one crack throughout the calorimeter.

I’d first test calibration on the existing 10k sample, then compare baseline and staggered geometries both before and after calibration. These remain proposals, with no claimed resolution gain yet.

[Detailed proposal added to PR #135](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/ecal10k-untiled-control/docs/validation/ecal10k-untiled/calibration-layout-options.md).

**UNTILED-PHYSVAL prospective review**, exact baseline **b9f5af38520ea83215587757b02cd090adc8fb8a**. Read all five pinned inputs and the prepared assignment/profile/skill. No writes, simulation, or delegation.

The control is scientifically useful if described as **continuous sensitive silicon within an explicitly defined sector face**, with these requirements frozen before transport:

- Remove/replace original active and guard silicon; do not overlay a second silicon volume. Record active area, total Si volume/mass, sensitive/passive reclassification, and material added in former gaps.
- Preserve absorber, hardware, layer depths, thicknesses and sector transforms wherever geometrically possible. Full sheets can intersect barrel slab-end frames, which span the cassette depth (`barrel_export.py:52`), and endcap supports (`edge_export.py:80`). Keep explicit exclusions or document every structural subtraction as an additional control change. Require native overlap/containment checks before bulk transport.
- The baseline module-local `x:-6,y:-6` fields at 5.5-mm pitch do **not** cover full sector slabs (`barrel_export.py:83`, `edge_export.py:110`). Provide sufficient addressing capacity or an explicitly documented alternative, verify no aliasing/out-of-range IDs, and preserve event deposited-energy sums. Baseline `EdgeGrid` also rejects positions outside module masks; its tile-specific mask tables cannot simply be reused for full sheets.

For the comparison:

1. Bind identical primary-input hashes, IDs, \(E,\eta,\phi\), origin, transport settings and per-event seeds. Match by ID, never physical output order.
2. Form tuples \((R_{\rm tiled},R_{\rm continuous})\), with \(R=\sum E_{\rm Si}/E_{\rm true}\), retaining all valid zero responses.
3. Use the **same resampled event-index vector** for both geometries and both angular projections in every bootstrap replicate. Retain each geometry’s width \(s(R)/\overline R\), paired difference \(w_{\rm continuous}-w_{\rm tiled}\), and optionally their ratio. Calculate intervals directly from paired replicate differences/ratios; do not combine marginal errors as independent.
4. Retain each geometry’s mean response, absolute sample SD, quantiles, zero fractions and counts. A smaller normalized width may partly reflect a larger mean after adding sensitive silicon.
5. Preserve the existing ten \(|\eta|\) bins and signed \(\pi/8\) folded-φ bins, defined from common primary truth. Use 5,000 whole-event replicas with a recorded comparison seed; undefined ratios/replicas remain explicit. Retain joint covariance of the comparison bins.
6. Require complete equal ID sets. If disk gating reduces the new run prospectively, compare against the **same baseline prefix/subset**, not the full 10k baseline.

Causal limits: shared primary IDs/seeds establish a matched-input simulation experiment, **not identical shower histories**. Geometry changes alter material interactions and random-number consumption. Do not require per-event response improvement or label differences as measurements of “tile inefficiency alone.” Added silicon, formerly passive guards becoming sensitive, unchanged mechanical seams/supports, and any necessary structural cuts all contribute. Residual seam features in the control are plausible and must remain visible.

Source basis: `BarrelCalorimeter.cpp` and `EdgeCalorimeter.cpp` define sensitive-volume ownership; `barrel_export.py:34–36,52,83,94–98`; `edge_export.py:40,61–62,80,110,118–124`; existing observable/bin/bootstrap contract at `docs/validation/ecal10k/protocol.md:44–85`. No change to these workflow/profile instructions since the previous reviewed baseline was found. Frozen control-source and result review remain outstanding; no design acceptance is implied.

events.text:
Reviewed **951d7b286c47882dc8068056e59d39abac1f31a4**, read-only. Scientific recommendation: pursue a small, event-dependent gap correction as a demonstrator; no quantitative improvement is established yet.

- Start with barrel/endcap scale factors and smooth corrections versus reconstructed impact distance to sector seams and sensor/service gaps. Add longitudinal shower features or an observable energy proxy only if held-out closure improves. Use reconstructed centroids in these ECAL-only samples; truth impact is an explicitly labelled oracle benchmark. True energy may supply training labels and evaluation denominators, never inference features.
- A constant positive gain within an angular bin cannot improve its reported width:  
  \[
  \frac{s(gR)}{\overline{gR}}=\frac{s(R)}{\bar R}.
  \]
  It changes scale only. Event-dependent corrections can remove predictable variation within bins, but cannot restore unobserved event fluctuations. Multiplicative calibration leaves zero-signal events at zero; assigning them prior-based energies would not recover a measurement.
- Keep calibration/tuning and final evaluation events independent. With only 10k events, use a low-dimensional exploratory model, preferably cross-fitting if reusing this sample. Validate subsequently at independent fixed energies and across signed η, sectors, seams and sensor centres. Report bias, full-response width, low-response tails and zero-response efficiency together. A reduced width alone can reflect regression toward the training spectrum.
- For uncertainty on a proposed improvement, resample raw/corrected versions of each held-out event together; propagate calibration-training uncertainty separately or by refitting within an outer bootstrap. Keep all generated events in acceptance denominators.

The existing observable is mixed-energy **raw** \(s(S/E_\mathrm{true})/\overline{S/E_\mathrm{true}}\), not established reconstructed fixed-energy resolution: `comparison.json:7–8`. My compact-data checks recovered 10,000 events in each projection and 42 tiled versus 37 continuous zero responses. The control therefore supplies motivation and a counterfactual comparison, not a promised calibration target or an isolated tiling contribution.

For layout options, avoid presenting existing axial staggering as new: DES031 already alternates −96/+96 mm (`DES-031:37–57`; `barrel.json:17–20`). A prospective comparison should instead examine tangential phase staggering or reduced aligned passive margins, including the documented sector-centre crack (`DES-031:97–101`; `barrel_layout.py:51–56`). Endcap masks currently repeat through depth (`DES-030:132–136`), so layer-dependent mask placement is another candidate. Changes need material and engineering accounting before attributing performance gains.

[CALICE arXiv:0811.2354, §5.2, printed pp. 7–10](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0811.2354) directly supports using shower-barycentre-dependent average gap corrections. It also states that individual gap fluctuations remain and uses a gap-excluded fiducial sample for subsequent resolution measurements. Its numerical performance cannot be transferred here.

Actual checks: pinned source inspection, comparison JSON hash **c25c0912…**, projection/count checks, and a numerical gain-invariance sanity check. No fits, simulation, file changes or acceptance/sign-off.

ECAL-OPTIONS-CALOTECH, read-only assessment at `951d7b286c47882dc8068056e59d39abac1f31a4`.

- **Separate slab staggering from board staggering.** Current slab phases −96/+96 mm differ by two 96 mm board pitches. They move service joints but leave corresponding interior board grids at the same phase. Simply changing to −48/+48 would also repeat the lattice.
- **Test independent 0/48 mm board phases across layers**, potentially cycling the axial and tangential phases over four layers. These are illustrative geometry candidates, with no predicted resolution improvement claimed.
- **Axial phasing is feasible for full slabs with repacking.** Nine rows currently span local centres −384..384 mm. A 48 mm shift away from the service bay retains nine rows within the full slab: PCB extent −479..383 mm versus a ±495 mm cavity and service bay 455..495 mm on the positive side. Short end slabs require separate packing checks.
- **Tangential phasing needs edge-board changes.** Available PCB side clearance is only 10.714 mm at layer 0, 1.741 mm at layer 18, and 1.440 mm at layer 40. A 48 mm translation therefore needs shaped edge boards, changed column counts, or revised service allocation. Preserve and recalculate silicon area, channel count, power and cooling budgets.
- **Endcaps need layer-dependent mask families.** Their existing parity-dependent row offsets repeat through all 48 layers. Alternate radial/tangential phases would require regenerated physical sensor/PCB masks, guards, ASIC placement, identifiers and aperture/service checks.
- **Full-depth sector cracks require a separate interface redesign.** Board phasing leaves the inherited seams, rails and absorber boundaries. Stepped or nonprojective interfaces need mechanical, clearance and service-routing assessment.

Sources: `barrel_layout.py:16–28,41–70`, `barrel.json`, `edge_layout.py:163–215`, DES-030/031. I byte-checked exercised layout dependencies against the pinned revision and ran the existing barrel builder to verify pitches, phase equivalence and clearances. No edits, transport runs or calibration fits.
